the local application, to solid tumours, of electric pulses, of sufficient intensity and duration, induces tumour blood flow changes.
the local application to tumours of short, intense electric pulses results in a progressive reduction of tumor blood flow with a concomitant increase in tumour cell death.
the application of electric pulses can induce a significant reduction in tumour blood flow and a corresponding increase in the cytotoxicity of the tumour.

developing new methods to control tumour blood flow and to exploit the resulting hypoxia for therapeutic gain.
the development of new methods for the treatment of solid tumours.
the use of electrical fields to modify blood flow in solid tumours.

the application of high voltage electric pulses to a solid tumour can induce changes in tumour blood flow, the magnitude of which is dependent upon pulse amplitude and duration.
tumour blood flow can be modified by the application of electric pulses and this may be a mechanism by which the electric pulses exert their cytotoxic effect.

electric pulses can be used as a local modality for inducing tumour blood flow changes and for enhancing the efficacy of anticancer agents.
the local application to a solid tumour of electric pulses of high voltage and short duration results in a significant decrease in tumour perfusion and an increase in the cytotoxicity of the tumour.

electric pulses are capable of modulating blood flow in tumours and that the effect is dependent on the pulse intensity.
